cp-bsit-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cp-bsit-aligned.explanation: The CLO practises using a modern computing tool (an IDE) to write, compile and debug Java programs, at Apply level.

cp-bsit-keyword.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsit-keyword.sourceQuote: Analyze complex problems, and identify and define the computing requirements
cp-bsit-keyword.targetQuote: Memorize the keywords and syntax of the Java language.
cp-bsit-keyword.explanation: The PO asks for analysing complex problems and identifying and defining computing requirements for a solution (Analyze). The CLO only asks to memorize keywords and syntax (Remember), which is a lower Bloom level. It has no analysis verb, and it does not mention problems, requirements or solution design. It shares only the computing field.
cp-bsit-keyword.draft: Analyze programming problems and identify and define the computing requirements, including inputs, processing and outputs, needed to design a Java solution.

cp-bsit-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsit-wrongpo.sourceQuote: Preserve and promote “Filipino historical and cultural heritage;
cp-bsit-wrongpo.targetQuote: Develop and test Java programs that use loops and conditional statements.
cp-bsit-wrongpo.explanation: The PO is about preserving and promoting Filipino historical and cultural heritage. The CLO is about developing and testing Java programs with loops and conditionals. The subject matter is unrelated, and the CLO has no verb or object concerning heritage or culture.
cp-bsit-wrongpo.draft: Develop and test Java programs that use loops and conditional statements to preserve and promote Filipino historical and cultural heritage, such as a program that catalogs and displays Philippine heritage sites or festivals.

cp-bsit-real3.label: ALIGNED
cp-bsit-real3.targetQuote: Collaborate effectively within multi-disciplinary and culturally diverse teams
cp-bsit-real3.explanation: The CLO collaborates in multi-disciplinary, culturally diverse teams to build Java solutions, which matches the PO's teamwork and subject.

cp-bsie-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsie-wrongpo.sourceQuote: Ability to function on multidisciplinary teams
cp-bsie-wrongpo.targetQuote: Develop a system requirements specification and a functional decomposition for an engineered system.
cp-bsie-wrongpo.explanation: The PO asks for the ability to function on multidisciplinary teams (a teamwork/collaboration competency). The CLO is about developing a requirements specification and functional decomposition, which is a technical design task. It has no teamwork verb (collaborate, contribute, work with), no mention of team roles or of multiple disciplines, and no team setting. The subject matter is different: the PO's object is team functioning, the CLO's is system documents. Bloom level: the PO is Apply, and the CLO is Create, so the level is not the problem, but verb and subject do not match.
cp-bsie-wrongpo.draft: Collaborate effectively in a multidisciplinary team to develop a system requirements specification and a functional decomposition for an engineered system, integrating the inputs of members from different disciplines and stakeholders.

cp-bsie-real2.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cp-bsie-real2.sourceQuote: design a system, component, or process to meet desired needs within realistic constraints
cp-bsie-real2.targetQuote: analyze, design, and optimize complex systems, integrating various components such as people, materials, technology, and information
cp-bsie-real2.explanation: The CLO shares the PO's design focus (design complex systems, integrating components), and its Bloom level (Analyze/Create) is not lower than the PO's (Create). Gaps: (1) it does not address meeting desired needs, since no needs or requirements are named; (2) it names no realistic constraints (economic, environmental, social, political, ethical, health and safety, manufacturability, sustainability); (3) it does not mention working in accordance with standards. The PO's object is a design that meets needs within constraints, while the CLO speaks only of optimizing complex systems.
cp-bsie-real2.draft: Apply critical and creative thinking skills to analyze, design, and optimize complex systems that meet stakeholder needs, integrating various components such as people, materials, technology, and information within realistic economic, environmental, social, ethical, health and safety, manufacturability, and sustainability constraints, in accordance with applicable standards.

cp-bscpe-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-aligned.targetQuote: Design and conduct experiments to characterize sensor accuracy
cp-bscpe-aligned.explanation: The CLO names designing and conducting experiments and analyzing and interpreting data, on sensor accuracy.

cp-bscpe-keyword.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-keyword.sourceQuote: Ability to design and conduct experiments, as well as to analyze and interpret data;
cp-bscpe-keyword.targetQuote: Discuss experiments in the history of sensor technology.
cp-bscpe-keyword.explanation: The CLO shares only the word 'experiments'. Its verb 'Discuss' is Understand level, below the PO's Create/Analyze level. It does not design or conduct experiments. It does not analyze or interpret data. It treats the history of sensor technology rather than doing experimental work on sensors or signal circuits.
cp-bscpe-keyword.draft: Design and conduct experiments on sensors and signal conversion circuits, and analyze and interpret the measurement data to evaluate sensor performance.

cp-bscpe-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-wrongpo.targetQuote: Calibrate a sensor and record its measurement tolerance.
cp-bscpe-wrongpo.explanation: The PO asks for effective communication. The CLO is about calibrating a sensor and recording its tolerance, which is a technical measurement task. It has no communicating verb (present, report, explain) and no audience or medium. Recording a value is not communicating effectively.
cp-bscpe-wrongpo.draft: Communicate effectively the calibration procedure and measurement tolerance of a sensor through a clear written technical report and an oral presentation to an engineering audience.

cp-bsit-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cp-bsit-aligned.explanation: Writing, compiling and debugging in an IDE applies a modern computing tool at Apply level.

cp-bsit-keyword.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsit-keyword.sourceQuote: Analyze complex problems, and identify and define the computing requirements
cp-bsit-keyword.targetQuote: Memorize the keywords and syntax of the Java language.
cp-bsit-keyword.explanation: The PO asks to analyze complex problems and identify and define computing requirements for a solution (Analyze). The CLO only asks to memorize Java keywords and syntax (Remember), which is a lower Bloom level and has no analysis verb. It also never mentions problems, requirements or designing a solution, so it shares only the programming topic.
cp-bsit-keyword.draft: Analyze programming problems, identify and define their computing requirements, and design Java solutions that apply the language's keywords and syntax correctly.

cp-bsit-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsit-wrongpo.sourceQuote: Preserve and promote “Filipino historical and cultural heritage
cp-bsit-wrongpo.targetQuote: Develop and test Java programs that use loops and conditional statements.
cp-bsit-wrongpo.explanation: The PO is about preserving and promoting Filipino historical and cultural heritage (Apply/Evaluate, cultural subject). The CLO is about developing and testing Java programs with loops and conditionals, a different subject with no cultural heritage content, verb or object.
cp-bsit-wrongpo.draft: Develop and test Java programs that use loops and conditional statements to present and promote Filipino historical and cultural heritage, such as a program that displays facts about local festivals or heritage sites.

cp-bsit-real3.label: ALIGNED
cp-bsit-real3.sourceQuote: Work effectively and independently in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural teams
cp-bsit-real3.targetQuote: Collaborate effectively within multi-disciplinary and culturally diverse teams
cp-bsit-real3.explanation: The CLO has students collaborate in multi-disciplinary and culturally diverse teams to build Java solutions, matching the PO's teamwork competency.

cp-bsie-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bsie-wrongpo.sourceQuote: Ability to function on multidisciplinary teams
cp-bsie-wrongpo.targetQuote: Develop a system requirements specification and a functional decomposition for an engineered system.
cp-bsie-wrongpo.explanation: The PO asks for the ability to function on multidisciplinary teams (a teamwork/collaboration competency, roughly Apply). The CLO is a technical Create-level task: developing a requirements specification and functional decomposition. It has (1) no teamwork or collaboration verb or competency, (2) no multidisciplinary context or team roles, and (3) a different subject, since it concerns the technical artifacts and not working with others. The CLO shares no key action or object with the PO.
cp-bsie-wrongpo.draft: Collaborate effectively on a multidisciplinary team to develop a system requirements specification and a functional decomposition for an engineered system, integrating the inputs of team members from different disciplines.

cp-bsie-real2.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cp-bsie-real2.sourceQuote: Ability to design a system, component, or process to meet desired needs within realistic constraints
cp-bsie-real2.targetQuote: Apply critical and creative thinking skills to analyze, design, and optimize complex systems
cp-bsie-real2.explanation: The CLO matches the PO's core: it designs and optimizes systems (Create level), and the object is an engineered system in the same discipline. Gaps: (1) it never mentions meeting desired needs or stakeholder needs; (2) it names none of the realistic constraints the PO lists (economic, environmental, social, political, ethical, health and safety, manufacturability, sustainability); (3) it does not mention working in accordance with standards.
cp-bsie-real2.draft: Apply critical and creative thinking skills to analyze, design, and optimize complex systems that integrate people, materials, technology, and information to meet desired stakeholder needs within realistic constraints such as economic, environmental, social, ethical, health and safety, manufacturability, and sustainability, in accordance with applicable standards.

cp-bscpe-aligned.label: ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-aligned.targetQuote: Design and conduct experiments to characterize sensor accuracy
cp-bscpe-aligned.explanation: The CLO has design, conduct, analyze and interpret on sensor experiments.

cp-bscpe-keyword.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-keyword.sourceQuote: Ability to design and conduct experiments, as well as to analyze and interpret data;
cp-bscpe-keyword.targetQuote: Discuss experiments in the history of sensor technology.
cp-bscpe-keyword.explanation: The CLO shares the word 'experiments' but its verb 'Discuss' is Understand level, below the PO's design/conduct (Create) and analyze/interpret (Analyze). It has no designing or conducting of experiments, no analysis or interpretation of data, and its subject is the history of sensor technology, not experimentation on sensors or signal circuits in this course.
cp-bscpe-keyword.draft: Design and conduct experiments on sensors and signal conversion circuits, and analyze and interpret the measurement data to draw conclusions about sensor performance.

cp-bscpe-wrongpo.label: NOT_ALIGNED
cp-bscpe-wrongpo.targetQuote: Calibrate a sensor and record its measurement tolerance.
cp-bscpe-wrongpo.explanation: The PO is about communicating effectively, but the CLO is about calibrating a sensor and recording tolerance. It has no communication verb (e.g. report, present, document for an audience) and no communication competency, and its Bloom level (Apply) is a technical procedure, not communication. Only a technical subject is shared, with no communication object.
cp-bscpe-wrongpo.draft: Communicate the results of a sensor calibration effectively by presenting the measurement tolerance in a written technical report and an oral presentation to engineering peers.
